chapter.name: Conic Sections
chapter.blurb: This chapter shows how a plane cutting a double-napped right circular cone produces the circle, ellipse, parabola and hyperbola, together with their degenerated cases. It then defines each curve by a geometric property and obtains its standard equation: the circle with centre (h, k), and the parabola, ellipse and hyperbola in standard position with centre or vertex at the origin. For these it studies the focus, directrix of a parabola, vertices, axes, eccentricity and latus rectum, and applies them to reflectors, arches and loci.

concepts.name: Sections of a cone and degenerated conics
concepts.description: How a plane cutting a double-napped right circular cone gives a circle, ellipse, parabola or hyperbola according to the angle beta it makes with the axis, and the degenerated sections when the plane passes through the vertex.
concepts.idea: A line m turning about a fixed line l at a constant angle alpha sweeps out a double-napped cone. A plane cutting it at angle beta to the axis gives a different curve for each range of beta.
concepts.rule: Plane not through the vertex: beta = 90 degrees circle; alpha < beta < 90 degrees ellipse; beta = alpha parabola; 0 <= beta < alpha hyperbola (both nappes). Plane through the vertex: point, straight line, or pair of intersecting lines for the same three ranges.
concepts.example: With alpha = 30 degrees, a plane missing the vertex at beta = 50 degrees gives an ellipse; at beta = 30 degrees a parabola; at beta = 10 degrees a hyperbola.

questions.q: The fixed point V at which the rotating line m meets the fixed vertical line l of a double-napped right circular cone is called the
questions.a: vertex of the cone

questions.q: The vertex separates a double-napped right circular cone into two parts. Each of these parts is called a ____. (Write one word.)
questions.a: nappe

questions.q: A plane cuts one nappe of a cone (not at the vertex) and makes an angle beta = 90 degrees with the axis of the cone. The section obtained is
questions.a: a circle

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a degenerated conic section obtained when a plane cuts a double-napped cone at its vertex?
questions.a: A circle
o: A pair of intersecting straight lines

questions.q: A plane cuts a double-napped right circular cone whose generator makes an angle alpha with its axis, not at the vertex, at an angle beta to the axis. In which case does the plane cut through BOTH nappes of the cone?
questions.a: When 0 <= beta < alpha, giving a hyperbola
o: When 0 <= beta < alpha, giving a hyperbola
When beta = alpha, giving a parabola
When alpha < beta < 90 degrees, giving an ellipse
When beta = 90 degrees, giving a circle

questions.q: A plane cuts a double-napped cone at its vertex with beta = alpha, so that the plane contains a generator and the section is a straight line. This straight line is the degenerated case of
questions.a: a parabola

questions.q: A plane cuts one nappe of a cone without passing through the vertex. In terms of alpha (the angle between a generator and the axis) and beta (the angle between the plane and the axis), explain the difference between the plane that gives an ellipse and the plane that gives a parabola.
questions.a: The section is an ellipse when alpha < beta < 90 degrees, that is, when the plane is inclined to the axis at an angle larger than the generator's angle but is not perpendicular to the axis. The section is a parabola when beta = alpha exactly, that is, when the plane makes the same angle with the axis as a generator does. In both cases the plane cuts only one nappe.
s: States the ellipse condition alpha < beta < 90 degrees
States the parabola condition beta = alpha

questions.q: A plane passes through the vertex of a double-napped right circular cone whose generator makes an angle alpha with its axis. The plane makes an angle beta with the axis, where alpha < beta <= 90 degrees. The section is
questions.a: a point
o: a pair of intersecting straight lines

questions.q: A plane that does not pass through the vertex cuts a double-napped right circular cone whose generator makes an angle alpha with its axis. As the angle beta between the plane and the axis is decreased steadily from 90 degrees to 0 degrees, the sections appear in the order
questions.a: circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola

questions.q: A generator of a cone makes an angle alpha = 35 degrees with its axis. A plane that does not pass through the vertex cuts the cone in a parabola. The angle beta between the plane and the axis is ____ degrees. (Write a whole number.)
For a cone, alpha = 30 degrees. A plane not passing through the vertex makes an angle beta = 50 degrees with the axis. The section is
questions.a: an ellipse

questions.q: For a cone, alpha = 40 degrees. A plane not passing through the vertex makes an angle beta = 25 degrees with the axis. The section is
questions.a: a hyperbola

questions.q: For a double-napped cone, alpha = 45 degrees. A plane passing through the vertex makes an angle beta = 20 degrees with the axis. The section is
questions.a: a pair of intersecting straight lines
o: a pair of intersecting straight lines

questions.q: For a cone, alpha = 25 degrees. A plane that does not pass through the vertex cuts the cone. Name the section, with a reason, when (i) beta = 25 degrees, (ii) beta = 60 degrees.
questions.a: (i) beta = alpha = 25 degrees, so the section is a parabola. (ii) 25 < 60 < 90, that is alpha < beta < 90 degrees, so the section is an ellipse.
s: (i) Parabola, because beta = alpha
(ii) Ellipse, because alpha < beta < 90 degrees

questions.q: A double-napped cone has alpha = 50 degrees. Name the section, giving the reason in terms of alpha and beta, for each plane: (i) a plane not through the vertex with beta = 90 degrees; (ii) a plane not through the vertex with beta = 10 degrees; (iii) a plane through the vertex with beta = 50 degrees.
questions.a: (i) beta = 90 degrees and the plane misses the vertex, so the section is a circle. (ii) 0 <= 10 < 50, that is 0 <= beta < alpha, so the plane cuts both nappes and the section is a hyperbola. (iii) The plane passes through the vertex with beta = alpha, so it contains a generator and the section is a straight line, the degenerated case of a parabola.
s: (i) Circle, since beta = 90 degrees
(ii) Hyperbola, since 0 <= beta < alpha (both nappes cut)
(iii) Straight line (degenerated parabola), since the plane is through the vertex with beta = alpha

questions.q: Assertion (A): A plane that cuts a double-napped cone (not at the vertex) with beta = alpha gives a parabola. Reason (R): When beta = alpha, the cutting plane passes through both nappes of the cone.
questions.a: A is true, R is false
o: A is true, R is false
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false, R is true

questions.q: Consider these statements. (I) A plane cutting a double-napped cone at its vertex with alpha < beta <= 90 degrees gives a single point. (II) A pair of intersecting straight lines is the degenerated case of a hyperbola. Which is or are correct?
questions.a: Both I and II

questions.q: A plane makes a fixed angle beta = 30 degrees with the axis of a double-napped cone and does not pass through the vertex. Cones with different values of alpha (the angle between a generator and the axis) are cut by this plane. Decide the type of section when (i) alpha = 20 degrees, (ii) alpha = 30 degrees, (iii) alpha = 55 degrees, and explain how the answer changes as alpha grows.
questions.a: (i) alpha = 20: here alpha < beta < 90 degrees (20 < 30 < 90), so the section is an ellipse. (ii) alpha = 30: beta = alpha, so the section is a parabola. (iii) alpha = 55: 0 <= beta < alpha (30 < 55), so the plane cuts both nappes and the section is a hyperbola. So for a fixed plane angle, a narrow cone (alpha less than beta) gives an ellipse, the cone with alpha equal to beta gives a parabola, and any wider cone (alpha greater than beta) gives a hyperbola.
s: (i) Ellipse, since alpha < beta < 90 degrees
(ii) Parabola, since beta = alpha
(iii) Hyperbola, since beta < alpha, with the general comparison of alpha with beta stated

questions.q: Meera says: 'Whenever a plane passes through the vertex of a double-napped cone, the section is just a single point.' Evaluate her statement.
questions.a: She is only partly right. The section is a point only when alpha < beta <= 90 degrees. If beta = alpha the plane contains a generator and the section is a straight line, and if 0 <= beta < alpha the section is a pair of intersecting straight lines. So her 'whenever' is wrong.
s: States that a point occurs only when alpha < beta <= 90 degrees
Gives the other cases: a straight line when beta = alpha, a pair of intersecting lines when beta < alpha

questions.q: Choose a value of alpha for a double-napped cone. Then choose three planes, none through the vertex, by giving their angles beta with the axis, so that the sections are an ellipse, a parabola and a hyperbola respectively. Justify each choice.
questions.a: For example take alpha = 40 degrees. Ellipse: beta = 70 degrees, because 40 < 70 < 90 (alpha < beta < 90 degrees). Parabola: beta = 40 degrees, because beta = alpha. Hyperbola: beta = 15 degrees, because 0 <= 15 < 40 (0 <= beta < alpha), so the plane cuts both nappes. (Any alpha strictly between 0 and 90 degrees with three betas satisfying these conditions earns full marks.)
s: Ellipse: a beta with alpha < beta < 90 degrees, justified
Parabola: beta = alpha, justified
Hyperbola: a beta with 0 <= beta < alpha, justified

concepts.name: Circle: equation, centre and radius
concepts.description: The circle as a set of points equidistant from a centre, its equation (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2, reading centre and radius by completing squares, and finding a circle from given conditions.
concepts.idea: Every point of a circle is at the same distance r from the centre (h, k); the distance formula turns that into an equation.
concepts.rule: (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2. To read centre and radius from an expanded equation, make the coefficients of x^2 and y^2 equal to 1 and complete the squares.

The radius of the circle x^2 + y^2 = 81 is ____. (Write a whole number.)
A circle is the set of all points in a plane that are
questions.a: equidistant from a fixed point in the plane
o: equidistant from a fixed point in the plane
equidistant from a fixed point and a fixed line in the plane
such that the sum of their distances from two fixed points is constant

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the circle (x - 3)^2 + (y + 4)^2 = 25 is FALSE?
questions.a: Its centre is (-3, 4)

questions.q: The centre of the circle (x + 2)^2 + (y - 7)^2 = 9 is
The equation of the circle with centre at the origin and radius 6 is
Explain why the equation (x - 1)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = 16 represents a circle of radius 4 and not of radius 16.
questions.a: The equation of a circle with centre (h, k) and radius r is (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2, so the right-hand side is the SQUARE of the radius. Here r^2 = 16, so r = 4 (radius is positive). The centre is (1, 2).
s: States that the right-hand side of the standard equation is r^2
Concludes r^2 = 16 gives r = 4

questions.q: The radius of the circle (x - 1)^2 + (y + 6)^2 = 20 is
questions.a: 2 sqrt(5)

questions.a: Inside the circle, because its distance from the centre is 5, which is less than 6

Outside the circle, because 4 + 3 = 7 is greater than 6
Outside the circle, because 4^2 + (-3)^2 = 25 is greater than the radius 6

questions.q: A circle with centre (1, 2) passes through the point (4, 6). Its radius is ____. (Write a whole number.)
The equation of the circle with centre (-3, 5) and radius 2 is
The centre of the circle x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 4y - 12 = 0 is
The radius of the circle x^2 + y^2 + 2x - 10y + 10 = 0 is
Find the centre and the radius of the circle 2x^2 + 2y^2 - 8x + 12y - 6 = 0.
questions.a: Divide by 2: x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 6y - 3 = 0. Completing the squares: (x^2 - 4x + 4) + (y^2 + 6y + 9) = 3 + 4 + 9, that is (x - 2)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 16. So the centre is (2, -3) and the radius is 4.
s: Divides by 2 and completes the squares to get (x - 2)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 16
States centre (2, -3) and radius 4

questions.q: Find the equation of the circle which passes through the points (5, 7) and (6, 0) and whose centre lies on the line x + y = 5.
questions.a: Let the circle be (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2. Through (5, 7): (5 - h)^2 + (7 - k)^2 = r^2. Through (6, 0): (6 - h)^2 + k^2 = r^2. Subtracting: 74 - 10h - 14k = 36 - 12h, so 2h - 14k + 38 = 0, that is h = 7k - 19. The centre lies on x + y = 5, so h + k = 5, giving 8k = 24, k = 3 and h = 2. Then r^2 = (6 - 2)^2 + 3^2 = 25. The circle is (x - 2)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 25.
s: Writes the two point conditions and the centre condition h + k = 5
Solves to get h = 2, k = 3
Finds r^2 = 25 and writes (x - 2)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 25

questions.q: Assertion (A): The circle x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 2y - 4 = 0 has radius 3. Reason (R): Completing the squares rewrites this equation as (x - 2)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = 9, which is of the form (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, R is false

questions.q: Consider these statements. (I) The circle (x + 1)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 49 has centre (1, -4). (II) The circle x^2 + y^2 = 50 passes through the point (5, -5). Which is or are correct?
questions.a: Only II

questions.q: A circle of radius 13 has its centre on the y-axis and passes through the point (5, 2). Find the equation of every such circle and explain why there is more than one.
questions.a: Let the centre be (0, k). Then (x - 0)^2 + (y - k)^2 = 169 and the point (5, 2) gives 25 + (2 - k)^2 = 169, so (2 - k)^2 = 144, 2 - k = 12 or -12, k = -10 or k = 14. The circles are x^2 + (y + 10)^2 = 169 and x^2 + (y - 14)^2 = 169. There are two because the condition is a quadratic equation in k with two real roots: the centre can be 12 units below or 12 units above the level y = 2 on the y-axis.
s: Takes centre (0, k) and forms 25 + (2 - k)^2 = 169
Solves to get k = -10 or k = 14 and writes both equations
Explains the two answers from the two roots of the quadratic in k

questions.q: Ravi says: 'The circle x^2 + y^2 + 6x - 8y = 0 has centre (3, -4) and radius 5.' Evaluate his statement.
questions.a: Completing the squares: (x^2 + 6x + 9) + (y^2 - 8y + 16) = 25, that is (x + 3)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 25 = {x - (-3)}^2 + (y - 4)^2. So the radius 5 is correct, but the centre is (-3, 4), not (3, -4). Ravi has the signs of both coordinates of the centre wrong.
s: Completes the squares to get (x + 3)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 25
Judges: radius 5 correct, centre should be (-3, 4)

questions.q: Construct the equation of a circle whose centre lies in the fourth quadrant and which passes through the origin. State the centre and the radius, write the equation in the form (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2, and verify that the origin lies on it.
questions.a: For example take the centre (6, -8), which is in the fourth quadrant. The radius is its distance from the origin: sqrt(36 + 64) = 10. Equation: (x - 6)^2 + (y + 8)^2 = 100. Check at (0, 0): 36 + 64 = 100, so the origin lies on the circle. (Any centre (h, k) with h > 0 and k < 0 and r^2 = h^2 + k^2 earns full marks.)
s: Chooses a centre (h, k) with h > 0, k < 0 and finds r as its distance from the origin
Writes the equation correctly with the right signs
Verifies that (0, 0) satisfies the equation

concepts.name: Parabola: definition and the four standard equations
concepts.description: The parabola as the set of points equidistant from a fixed line (directrix) and a fixed point (focus), its axis and vertex, the four standard equations with vertex at the origin, and which way each opens.
concepts.idea: Each point of a parabola is as far from the focus as from the directrix. Putting the vertex at the origin and the axis along a coordinate axis gives four simple equations.
concepts.rule: y^2 = 4ax opens right, y^2 = -4ax opens left, x^2 = 4ay opens upwards, x^2 = -4ay opens downwards (a > 0). A y^2 term means the axis is the x-axis; an x^2 term means the axis is the y-axis.
concepts.example: A parabola symmetric about the y-axis through (2, -3) opens downwards: 4 = -4a(-3) gives a = 1/3, so 3x^2 = -4y.

questions.q: By definition, a parabola is the set of all points in a plane that are
questions.a: equidistant from a fixed line and a fixed point (not on the line) in the plane
o: equidistant from a fixed line and a fixed point (not on the line) in the plane
equidistant from a fixed point in the plane
such that the sum of their distances from two fixed points is constant
such that the difference of their distances from two fixed points is constant

questions.q: The fixed line used in the definition of a parabola is called the ____ of the parabola. (Write one word.)
questions.a: directrix

questions.q: The point of intersection of a parabola with its axis is called the
questions.a: vertex

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four standard equations of a parabola with vertex at the origin (a > 0)?
The parabola y^2 = -4ax, where a > 0, opens
questions.a: to the left

questions.q: If the standard equation of a parabola has an x^2 term (for example x^2 = 4ay), then its axis of symmetry is along
questions.a: the y-axis

questions.q: Explain why the parabola y^2 = 4ax, with a > 0, has no point whose x-coordinate is negative.
questions.a: For every point (x, y) on the curve, y^2 = 4ax. Since y^2 is never negative, 4ax >= 0, and as a > 0 this forces x >= 0. So x can be zero or positive but never negative; the curve lies in the first and fourth quadrants (and passes through the origin).
s: Uses y^2 >= 0 to get 4ax >= 0
Concludes x >= 0 because a > 0

questions.q: The parabola x^2 = -20y
questions.a: has the y-axis as its axis of symmetry and opens downwards
o: has the y-axis as its axis of symmetry and opens downwards
has the y-axis as its axis of symmetry and opens upwards

Which of the following parabolas opens upwards?
A parabola has its vertex at the origin and its axis along the x-axis, and it passes through the point (-2, 4). Its equation is
A parabola has its vertex at the origin, is symmetric about the y-axis and passes through the point (6, -3). Its equation is
Using the definition of a parabola (and the distance formula), derive the equation of the parabola whose focus is (3, 0) and whose directrix is the line x = -3.
questions.a: Let P(x, y) be a point of the parabola. Its distance from the focus is sqrt((x - 3)^2 + y^2) and its distance from the directrix x = -3 is sqrt((x + 3)^2). Setting these equal and squaring: (x - 3)^2 + y^2 = (x + 3)^2, so x^2 - 6x + 9 + y^2 = x^2 + 6x + 9, giving y^2 = 12x.
s: Equates the distance from (3, 0) to the distance from the line x = -3
Squares and simplifies to y^2 = 12x

questions.q: A parabola has its vertex at the origin, is symmetric about the y-axis and passes through the point (4, -2). (i) Decide whether it opens upwards or downwards, with a reason. (ii) Find its equation. (iii) Find the y-coordinate of the points on it whose x-coordinate is 12.
questions.a: (i) Symmetric about the y-axis with vertex at the origin, so the form is x^2 = 4ay or x^2 = -4ay. The point (4, -2) has a negative y-coordinate (fourth quadrant), so the parabola opens downwards: x^2 = -4ay. (ii) Substituting (4, -2): 16 = -4a(-2) = 8a, so a = 2 and the equation is x^2 = -8y. (iii) At x = 12: 144 = -8y, so y = -18.
s: Chooses the form x^2 = -4ay (opens downwards) with the reason
Finds a = 2 and the equation x^2 = -8y
Finds y = -18 when x = 12

questions.q: Assertion (A): The parabola y^2 = -6x opens downwards. Reason (R): If the standard equation of a parabola has a y^2 term, then its axis of symmetry is along the x-axis.

Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.q: Three parabolas with vertex at the origin are given: P1: y^2 = 7x, P2: x^2 = -3y, P3: y^2 = -x. (i) State the axis of symmetry and the direction of opening of each. (ii) Decide, with working, which of them passes through the point (-4, 2). (iii) Explain how part (i) could have told you in advance that P1 cannot pass through (-4, 2).
questions.a: (i) P1 has a y^2 term and a positive coefficient of x: axis along the x-axis, opens to the right. P2 has an x^2 term and a negative coefficient of y: axis along the y-axis, opens downwards. P3 has a y^2 term and a negative coefficient of x: axis along the x-axis, opens to the left. (ii) At (-4, 2): P1: y^2 = 4 but 7x = -28, no. P2: x^2 = 16 but -3y = -6, no. P3: y^2 = 4 and -x = 4, yes. Only P3 passes through (-4, 2). (iii) P1 opens to the right, so every point on it has x >= 0; a point with x = -4 cannot lie on it.

The equation is x^2/1 - y^2/3 = 1, that is 3x^2 - y^2 = 3. c = 2a = 2, so the foci are (2, 0) and (-2, 0). The point (2, 3) has the same x-coordinate as the focus (2, 0), so it lies on the line through that focus perpendicular to the transverse axis, and it is on the hyperbola; hence it is an end of that latus rectum (whose length 2b^2/a = 6 agrees with the ends (2, 3) and (2, -3)).
